title: SEMICON West 2026: After the Toast, the Hard Questions
gist: Lauro Rizzatti's SEMICON West 2026 recap says the chip industry crossed $1 trillion in annual revenue years early, with WSTS projecting about $1.66 trillion for 2026 on memory up about 300%. The conversation has turned to $2 trillion and whether fabs, power and people can keep up, with agentic AI bridging design and manufacturing.

insights.claim: The industry has already crossed $1 trillion in annual revenue, almost four years ahead of earlier projections.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Demand has pulled the trillion-dollar milestone far forward.
insights.quote: almost four years ahead of earlier projections

insights.claim: WSTS put first-half 2026 sales at $702 billion, double a year earlier, and its August update points to roughly $1.66 trillion for the full year, with memory up about 300%.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Memory pricing and volume is the main driver of the surge.
insights.quote: its August update points to roughly $1.66 trillion for the full year, with memory up about 300%

insights.claim: SEMI chose the theme 'the road from one trillion to two', and the show's talk had already moved from celebrating to whether fabs, power and people can keep up.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Constraints on power, capacity and talent, not demand, are the binding limits.
insights.quote: Nobody on stage was celebrating for long.

insights.claim: Rizzatti describes an 'enviable problem': demand is extraordinary and the hard part is meeting it within limits of power, cost and production readiness.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Supply-side bottlenecks favor equipment, packaging and power suppliers.

themes.theme: AI economics in chip design versus manufacturing

insights.claim: Synopsys CEO Sassine Ghazi described embedding agentic AI across the company's whole product portfolio, raising the question of proving silicon comes out right when AI designs the hardware it runs on.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: EDA is moving toward agentic flows, making verification trust the key issue.
insights.quote: Speed is the easy part to demonstrate. Proving that the silicon comes out right is harder.

insights.claim: Wally Rhines argued chip design adopted AI about four years before manufacturing because manufacturing involves orders of magnitude more parameters, and training foundation models on that data would need hyperscale data centers.
insights.speaker: Wally Rhines
insights.so_what: Data scale explains the lag in fab AI adoption.
insights.quote: explained why chip design took up AI some four years before manufacturing did

insights.claim: Agentic AI sidesteps the need for one giant model by splitting problems into narrow tasks handled by smaller specialized models, and manufacturing is quickly taking advantage of this.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Fab AI adoption may accelerate without hyperscale training costs.

insights.claim: An IEEE panel moderated by Rhines asked what agentic AI costs and returns; the real test is whether it demonstrably cuts development time and manufacturing cost without compromising correctness, not how many tasks it automates.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: ROI proof, not task count, will determine agentic AI spending in semis.
insights.quote: What does agentic AI actually cost, and what does it return?
insights.locator: Agentic AI: What It Costs, What It Returns

insights.claim: A full day on design at SEMICON West, organized by the ESD Alliance with TSMC's L.C. Lu opening, led to the lesson that design now depends on packaging, process and fab data, and the fab needs earlier sight of designer intent.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Design-manufacturing convergence expands the market for data-sharing and trust layers.

themes.theme: Packaging, supply chain and the geographic shift

insights.claim: The Advanced Packaging and Heterogeneous Integration Summit tied chiplets, 2.5D/3D, HBM and co-packaged optics to thermal density, inspection, yield and equipment readiness: an AI architecture is only as good as the memory, interconnect and cooling that can be built at sensible cost.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Packaging equipment and inspection are growth beneficiaries.

insights.claim: Four topics ran through almost every room: AI scaling, heterogeneous integration, advanced manufacturing and supply-chain resilience, supported by a Geopolitical Summit and a panel on AI-powered resilience for the $2T supply chain.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Resilience is now coupled to the AI scaling narrative.

insights.claim: The next SEMICON West opens in Phoenix in March 2027, which Rizzatti reads as the show following the fabs.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Domestic US fab buildout is reshaping industry event geography.
insights.quote: the show is following the fabs

insights.claim: SEMICON West expected over 35,000 attendees across more than 1,500 booths and over 700 exhibitors, with sessions on large domestic fab projects featuring Micron, the U.S. Department of Commerce and Entegris.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Policy and state partnership remain central to US fab expansion.
